clue.text: Finished on top

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to the same little word: completed, and positioned higher than something else.

clue.text: Quiet lift gets approval

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play softly
to lift is to raise

explanation.surface: A hushed promotion at work is met with approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is spoken approval of someone, so the noun swaps cleanly for the definition.

clue.text: Builder's first to leave tip with a load

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word Builder's

explanation.surface: A builder leaves first after getting a tip along with a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, figuratively a load one carries.

clue.text: He drowned in the Aegean, one tenor after love rejected

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: love being rejected means the zero letter is thrown out of the singer's name

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was the most famous operatic tenor
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tenor who lost in love meets a tragic end in Greek waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on Greek myth rather than a dictionary sense; 'He' is the mythical figure, not a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too near the sun, his wax wings melted and he fell into the sea and drowned.

clue.text: Direct insurance on clipped wagon, last in fleet

indicators.note: a clipped word has its end trimmed off, so the last letter of the wagon word goes

parts.note: a truck is a goods wagon on the railway

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the word fleet

explanation.surface: A fleet manager directs that insurance be taken out on a shortened wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone is to direct or order them, both verbs of giving commands.

clue.text: Not where they serve in doubles?

definitions.text: Not where they serve in doubles?

parts.words: Not where they serve in doubles?
parts.note: the surface reads as tennis, where doubles are paired matches; really it is a pub for unattached people, where doubles are large measures of spirits

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on tennis: a place named for singles would not host doubles, yet such a bar happily serves double measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar aimed at unattached people looking to meet, playfully contrasted with doubles in tennis and drinks.

clue.text: Morality play always confused many

parts.note: always means ever, as in for ever

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A medieval drama always bewildered a crowd of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyman is the famous fifteenth-century English morality play about a man summoned by Death.

clue.text: Photograph sucker pumped full of lead

explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is a police photograph of a suspect's face, a specific kind of picture.

clue.text: Outspoken Voltaire tale abridged

parts.note: Candide is Voltaire's satirical novella

explanation.surface: A frank critic judges a shortened edition of a Voltaire story.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and outspoken, saying what one thinks openly.

clue.text: Testing hearing

definitions.meaning: testing in the sense of difficult or taxing, as a testing day
a hearing is a court case, putting someone on trial

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a trying time is a testing one, and trying a case means giving it a court hearing.

clue.text: Plan building great sty

indicators.note: building suggests the letters are put together into a new structure

clue.text: Novel recorder's no good? Article little-known

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is removed from the legal officer's title

parts.note: in England a recorder is a part-time judge in the Crown Court
the is the definite article
something little-known is obscure

explanation.surface: A recording artist is dismissed as a dud in an article about obscure figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' looks like a tape machine or flute but is a British judicial title, a part-time judge; 'no' then drops the G (good) from JUDGE. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jude the Obscure is Thomas Hardy's final novel, published in 1895.

clue.text: Frank's unqualified

definitions.meaning: frank means open and forthcoming, holding nothing back
unqualified means without limitation, as in unqualified support

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: an open manner holding nothing back, and approval given without any conditions.

clue.text: There's nothing, nothing like an egg

parts.note: O is the round symbol for nothing or zero
a void is emptiness, nothing at all

explanation.surface: An empty shell contains nothing at all, just like an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, so it substitutes for the adjectival phrase like an egg.

clue.text: Badly behaved child runs into club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.definitionFit: A brat is an unruly, spoilt or badly behaved child.

clue.text: Drink one with a girl after time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone shares a drink with a girl once it is time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur, so it is a brand of drink.

clue.text: Bad time back in platoon?

parts.note: bad quality is poor

explanation.surface: A platoon goes through a rough patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of soldiers, comparable to a platoon, hence the query marking an approximate match.

clue.text: Attendant, worker with tattoo, perhaps

clue.text: Punch's dog in play involving bishop

explanation.walkthrough: In the British Punch and Judy puppet show, Punch's dog is called Toby.
explanation.definitionFit: Toby is the traditional dog in British Punch and Judy seaside puppet shows.

clue.text: Long-haired boxer's blue tale?

parts.note: long, rough hair is shaggy
a boxer is a breed of dog, with the possessive s
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: A long-haired boxer dog tells a rude story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like rude but is the Conservative party colour; 'boxer' is a dog breed, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaggy dog story is a long rambling tale with a pointless ending; the query flags the specific kind.

clue.text: Herds crossing eastern river

clue.text: Composer after end of concert tour
